title.analysis: Authentic title "How Much Car Your Salary Actually Buys You (Shocking)" promises salary-based purchase limits. The script delivers four salary tiers with 10%/8% rules, but its price ranges are lower than its own payment assumptions support and the $150K figure changes between sections. "(Shocking)" is a generic intensifier.

script.stored_text_completeness: All 17999 canonical characters read sequentially in full in 1 bounded ranges; auto-generated untimed text; stored text ends on the subscribe call ("...smart money decisions absolutely will.") with no separate sign-off; ASR garbles several figures ("23 12%", "$48" for about $408, "$21,66" and "a4 million") and words ("carpor", "sixf figureure", "wealth-b buildinging"); audio, timed delivery and editing unverified.
script.opening_words: Have you ever walked onto a car lot feeling financially confident only to leave three hours later wondering if you just signed your life away for the next seven years? You're not alone. You know, right now the average American is paying over $700 a month for their car payment. And that's before we even talk about insurance, gas, and the soul crushing realization that their shiny new ride lost 20% of its value the moment they drove it off
script.ending_words: lets you shop around 40,000. These aren't suggestions. They're financial survival guidelines. Your future wealthy self will thank you for driving that boring reliable car while everyone else is drowning in payments. If this video just saved you from years of financial regret, smash that subscribe button and check out my video on building wealth in your 20s because cars don't make you rich, but smart money decisions absolutely will.
script.analysis: Full 17999 canonical characters read. A single-narrator explainer with composites Sarah and Mike: hook on average payments and depreciation, 20/4/10 and 20/3/8 rules, total cost of ownership and depreciation, four salary tiers ($50K, $75K, $100K, $150K), Sarah vs Mike, reliable cheap cars, dealer add-ons, opportunity cost, Buffett, image-driven buyers, loan-term arithmetic, recap and subscribe. Several headline calculations reproduce; tier price ranges, Sarah's figures and the loan-term totals do not.
